instruction: Looks reasonable. Go ahead, while also brainstorm and investigate if there's other more elegant and general solution for this (e.g., some neural/probablistic approach?).

ideas.title: Pretrained DRS parsing with a deterministic logic converter
ideas.one_liner: Use an existing logic-oriented neural parser rather than infer full semantics from verbal SRL.
ideas.hypothesis: Explicit scope boxes may reduce quote, negation and modal attachment errors.
ideas.proposed_method: Reuse a released DRS parser if weights are available; translate its boxes, referents and conditions into the existing logical form. Keep original-span alignments and refuse unsupported conversions.
ideas.minimal_experiment: First establish checkpoint access, then compare 30 fixed scope-heavy claims with the current compiler.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Zhang, Bouma and Bos 2025 (p10); Pustejovsky et al. 2019 (p11)

feasibility.compute: 1-6 GPU-hours for inference; checkpoint availability unconfirmed (planning estimate)
feasibility.data: Existing claims; structured meaning references still needed

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: better scope without extra training. Negative: unavailable weights or conversion errors dominate.

ideas.title: A small source-conditioned neural ranker
ideas.one_liner: Score whether each candidate graph preserves the source sentence.
ideas.hypothesis: A cross-encoder can use lexical roles and scope rather than compiler scores alone.
ideas.proposed_method: Encode the original sentence together with a deterministic rendering of a candidate graph. Train only a small head or a compact text cross-encoder on checked positive/negative graph pairs; keep the candidate generator fixed.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Measure leave-video-out ranking on checked pairs, with majority, likelihood and simple edit-cost controls. Do not claim performance from resubstitution on 63 outputs.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.

feasibility.data: At least 100-200 newly checked candidate pairs; current 63 judgments are insufficient for a credible held-out claim

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: ranks faithful alternatives above role/scope errors. Negative: lexical leakage or no gain over simple controls.

ideas.title: Marginalize over alternative logical forms
ideas.one_liner: Represent parse uncertainty as mutually exclusive choices before evidence verification.
ideas.hypothesis: Retaining ambiguity may improve calibration compared with choosing one parse or OR-ing all readings.
ideas.proposed_method: Use one parser to produce a bounded deduplicated candidate set, learn/calibrate source-only weights and retain probability for no adequate parse. Compile the categorical parse choice and shared evidence variables into probabilistic logic.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Check the mixture semantics on authored native examples, then compare calibration and cost on source-disjoint manually judged candidates.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Krishnamurthy et al. 2016 (p6); Park et al. 2024 (p5)

feasibility.compute: CPU engineering checks; 1-6 GPU-hours for candidate generation (planning estimate)
feasibility.data: Checked candidate meanings and source-disjoint calibration labels

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: uncertainty tracks genuine ambiguity. Negative: confidently weighted wrong parses or no faithful candidate; report both.

ideas.title: Generate logical structure through typed grammar actions
ideas.one_liner: Constrain the decoder using the current partial AST and well-formedness conditions.
ideas.hypothesis: Earlier type/scope checks can reduce wasted invalid candidates.
ideas.proposed_method: Generate create-node, bind-argument and attach-scope actions with a source-specific symbol table. Use one incremental AST checker rather than per-word post-processing.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare one fixed action decoder and current JSON edits on the same 40 failures, checking full meaning and latency separately.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Scholak et al. 2021 (p1); Poesia et al. 2022 (p2); Nagy et al. 2026 (p12)

feasibility.data: Current parser inputs and checked outputs

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: fewer malformed outputs at equal meaning accuracy. Negative: types pass while relationships remain wrong.

ideas.title: Contrastive consistency across related claims
ideas.one_liner: Use known local meaning changes to test or train the semantic parser.
ideas.hypothesis: A parser that tracks controlled role, scope and source changes has fewer spurious readings.
ideas.proposed_method: Create reviewed subject/object, quote/world and negation contrasts; require equivalent paraphrases to yield equivalent graphs and meaning changes to affect the corresponding subgraph. Use consistency as training evidence only after checking examples.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Construct 30-50 contrast pairs across new videos and measure graph differences, not only verdict agreement.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.

feasibility.data: New manually checked contrasts; some earlier edits can seed development only

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: exposes systematic bindings and supplies useful local labels. Negative: transformations are unfaithful or the parser can satisfy shallow lexical tests.

ideas.title: Soft neural scores for relationships with global constraints
ideas.one_liner: Treat parser links as uncertain features rather than mandatory edges.
ideas.hypothesis: Soft structural prediction can override a wrong dependency edge while maintaining a valid graph.
ideas.proposed_method: Score candidate argument, modifier and scope links with a frozen encoder plus small classifiers. Apply hard constraints only for declarations/types/acyclic scopes and globally normalize or decode compatible structures.
ideas.minimal_experiment: On checked constructions, compare hard dependency constraints with soft scores and identical graph candidates.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Cheng and Lapata 2018 (p7); Krishnamurthy et al. 2016 (p6)

feasibility.data: Several hundred checked link/scope labels; not obtainable from pass/fail errors alone

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: corrects annotation disagreements. Negative: weak labels cannot identify the intended graph or search becomes costly.

ideas.title: Repair partial ASTs while preserving checked fragments
ideas.one_liner: Separate missing structure from already validated local constraints.
ideas.hypothesis: Structural repair can recover claims without unnecessarily regenerating complete graphs.
ideas.proposed_method: Keep actual partial compiler state and source anchors; allow bounded subtree replacement. Preserve only independently checked fragments as hard constraints, keeping parser-only suggestions defeasible.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Evaluate the fixed 20 existing-draft/20 partial-draft diagnostic with generic versus compiler feedback; inspect every complete output.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Poesia et al. 2022 (p2); Nagy et al. 2026 (p12)

feasibility.data: Current real claims and saved annotations

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: new faithful repairs from saved partial state. Negative: more executability without preserved meaning.

ideas.title: Calibrate selective acceptance on unseen source videos
ideas.one_liner: Measure coverage only at a checked reliability level.
ideas.hypothesis: Abstention can expose the large gap between valid structure and faithful meaning.
ideas.proposed_method: Combine source-only parser confidence, typed-check outcomes and candidate disagreement into a calibrated acceptance score. Keep meaning uncertainty separate from insufficient media evidence.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Collect 100-200 video-disjoint meaning judgments; report coverage versus error and failures to find a faithful candidate.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Park et al. 2024 (p5); Cheng and Lapata 2018 (p7)

feasibility.compute: CPU calibration; 1-2 GPU-hours for fixed candidate features (planning estimate)
feasibility.data: New video-disjoint labels; development judgments cannot establish calibration guarantees

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: useful coverage at low error. Negative: no threshold transfers across video sources; disclose the shift.

ideas.title: Bidirectional generation as a faithfulness diagnostic
ideas.one_liner: Compare the original sentence with a text rendering of each candidate graph.
ideas.hypothesis: Back-generation may reveal omitted or swapped relationships that word coverage misses.
ideas.proposed_method: Use a frozen graph-to-text model or a deterministic rendering and bidirectional text entailment. Treat this as an auxiliary diagnostic; it can repair a bad graph silently or miss fine distinctions.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare its scores against existing checked role/scope errors and an edit-cost baseline without tuning on the final test videos.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Cheng and Lapata 2018 (p7); Bevilacqua et al. 2021 (p9)

feasibility.data: Checked graph pairs and original sentences

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: flags some errors cheaply. Negative: fluent back-generation hides wrong structure, so never a proof.

ideas.title: A flat typed semantic graph as the common output
ideas.one_liner: Let one neural decoder emit nodes and labelled edges, then compile deterministically.
ideas.hypothesis: Explicit IDs and separate scope edges may be easier to generate than deeply nested JSON.
ideas.proposed_method: Use entity/event/operator nodes with argument and context edges; validate reachability, declaration and scope before converting to the existing logical form. Keep this a single parser path, not selection among frontend models.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare equivalent flat and nested output formats on the same fixed claims, with identical source input and reviewed meanings.
ideas.novelty_rationale: This is a candidate frontend/evaluation design, not a claim that the underlying established method is new. A paper contribution would require a controlled finding about typed multimodal verification and binding errors.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Raspanti et al. 2025 (p3); Bevilacqua et al. 2021 (p9)

feasibility.data: Current claims and matched graph references

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: less duplication or invalid nesting. Negative: only a serialization change with no semantic gain.

ideas.title: A fixed AMR frontend with compositional logical semantics
ideas.one_liner: Use the existing neural AMR output as the meaning graph and apply a formal recursive translation.
ideas.hypothesis: Some current failures are caused by reconstructing missing semantic links from verbal SRL; cached AMR already supplies these links.
ideas.proposed_method: Keep a single frozen BART AMR frontend. Translate its concepts, roles, identity and explicitly supported scope operators compositionally into the existing logic. Use source-span evidence and refuse unsupported meanings; do not select the better frontend separately for each claim.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Use the existing AMR cache on the same40 cases, with checked reference meanings; compare source fidelity and typed-scope preservation before any broader rollout.
ideas.novelty_rationale: AMR-to-FOL is established by Bos2016 and Lai etal2020. The useful result would be whether this frontend reduces our conversion errors at a fixed annotation/compute cost; it is not the paper contribution by itself.
ideas.closest_prior_work: Bos2016 (p16); Lai, Donatelli and Pustejovsky2020 (p15); Bevilacqua etal2021 (p9)

ideas.expected_outcome: Positive: preserves the wind-speed and attribution structures without parser retraining. Negative: AMR errors or scope gaps dominate; the robot and charger examples already show that risk.
